discovery: Prediction and discovery of magic-angle flat bands and correlated superconducting and insulating states in twisted bilayer graphene, founding the field of moire quantum matter

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Formerly University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: 2D materials and moire quantum matter
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that two graphene sheets twisted by about 1.1 degrees develop nearly flat electronic bands, where interactions should dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers confirmed this, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. The results have been reproduced by many groups worldwide. Their work made the twist angle a new control parameter, turning van der Waals stacks into tunable quantum simulators of strongly correlated electrons. It opened the field of moire quantum matter: orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, generalized Wigner crystals, moire excitons and, more recently, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states and fractional Chern insulators at zero magnetic field. Few recent discoveries have given so many laboratories access to so much new physics. It is a clear case of close interplay between theory and experiment producing a new platform.
